Reason: The lateral chest X-ray (Figure 1) demonstrates a large, homogeneous, well-circumscribed opacity that forms an obtuse angle with the chest wall, a classic radiographic sign of an extrapulmonary (pleural or chest wall) mass rather than an intrapulmonary lesion. This is confirmed by the axial CT images (Figures 2 and 3), which show a large, smooth-margined pleural-based mass.
